source.text: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ שִׁ֣יר מִזְמ֑וֹרהָרִ֥יעוּ לֵ֝אלֹהִים כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director. A song. A psalm. Shout to God, all the earth!

en.L: For the director: a song; a psalm. Shout to God, all the earth!
en.B: For the music director. A song. A psalm. Raise a shout to God, all the earth!
en.R: For the leader of the music. A song, a psalm. Shout out to God with joy, everyone on earth!

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: a song, a psalm: two words for a song
decisions.reason: The first word (shir) is the ordinary word for a song; the second (mizmor) is a song sung to music. Psalms 65-68 all carry both words. Unlike most psalms near it, this one names no author.

decisions.choice: shout: a loud cry of joy and acclaim
decisions.reason: The verb (rua', causative) is the shout raised for a king or for victory (47:2; Numbers 23:21). Here the whole earth acclaims God as King.

decisions.choice: with joy
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of shout it is (m3).

source.text: זַמְּר֥וּ כְבֽוֹד־שְׁמ֑וֹ שִׂ֥ימוּ כָ֝ב֗וֹד תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Sing praise [to the] glory of his name; make glory his praise.

en.L: Sing praise [to] the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise glory!
en.B: Make music to the honor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} praise that is full of glory!
en.R: Sing and play music about how great {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name is. Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a way that shows how wonderful {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is!

decisions.choice: sing praise: make music, often with instruments
decisions.reason: The verb (zamar) means to sing or play music in praise; the noun mizmor ("psalm") comes from it.

decisions.choice: make glory his praise: give him glorious praise
decisions.reason: The words say "set glory, his praise": either make his praise glorious, or make his glory the subject of praise. Both say that the praise should match who he is.

decisions.choice: the glory of his name: the honor of who he is
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known (20:2).

decisions.choice: in a way that shows how wonderful he is
decisions.reason: Readable says what glorious praise is (m2).

source.text: אִמְר֣וּ לֵ֭אלֹהִים מַה־נּוֹרָ֣א מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ בְּרֹ֥ב עֻ֝זְּךָ֗ יְֽכַחֲשׁ֖וּ לְךָ֣ אֹיְבֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Say to God, How awesome [are] your works! In [the] greatness of your strength your enemies cringe to you.

en.L: Say to God, "How awesome [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works! In the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies cringe before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Say to God, "How fearsome are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} deeds! Because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength is so great, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies cower and fawn before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Tell God, "The things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do are amazing! You are so strong that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies bow down to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, even if they do not mean it.

decisions.choice: awesome: causing fear and wonder
decisions.reason: The word (nora') describes what makes people tremble in awe; it returns in verse 5.

decisions.choice: cringe: come crawling with false submission
decisions.reason: The verb (kachash) means to deceive or deny. Used of defeated enemies (18:45; Deuteronomy 33:29) it means bowing low to the victor with flattery that is not meant.

decisions.choice: a quotation that runs to verse 4
decisions.reason: The words the earth is told to say to God run to the end of verse 4, before the Selah.

decisions.choice: even if they do not mean it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the sense of the verb (m2).

source.text: כָּל־הָאָ֤רֶץ׀יִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לְ֭ךָ וִֽיזַמְּרוּ־לָ֑ךְ יְזַמְּר֖וּ שִׁמְךָ֣ סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: All the earth will bow down to you and will sing praise to you; they will sing praise [to] your name. Selah.

en.L: All the earth will bow down to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and sing praise to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; they will sing praise [to] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name." Selah
en.B: The whole earth bows low to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and sings to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; they make music to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name." Selah
en.R: Everyone on earth will worship {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. They will sing songs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, songs that honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name." Selah

decisions.choice: will bow down: what the earth does, or should do
alternatives: let all the earth bow down
decisions.reason: The verbs can state what happens or will happen, or express a wish ("let them bow down"). In the mouth of the singers it is both a claim and a call.

decisions.choice: bow down: worship by bowing to the ground
decisions.reason: The verb (shachah) is the bow of a subject before a king, the outward act of worship.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: לְכ֣וּ וּ֭רְאוּ מִפְעֲל֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֑ים נוֹרָ֥א עֲ֝לִילָ֗ה עַל־בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Come and see [the] works of God, awesome [in] deed toward [the] sons of man.

en.L: Come and see the works of God, awesome [in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] deeds toward the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}.
en.B: Come and look at the works of God, how fearsome {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dealings are with humankind!
en.R: Come, look at the things God has done! What {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does among people is amazing.

decisions.choice: deed: an act, a way of dealing with someone
decisions.reason: The word ('alilah) is a deed, often a mighty act of God in history (77:13; 78:11). Verse 6 says which deeds are meant.

decisions.choice: toward the sons of man: in his dealings with people
alternatives: awesome to the sons of man
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "toward" or "over": God's deeds are done to people, or tower over them. Either way, all humankind is meant to see them.

decisions.choice: the sons of man: human beings
decisions.reason: As in 11:4, the phrase means people in general.

source.text: הָ֤פַךְ יָ֨ם׀לְֽיַבָּשָׁ֗ה בַּ֭נָּהָר יַֽעַבְר֣וּ בְרָ֑גֶל שָׁ֝֗ם נִשְׂמְחָה־בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He turned [the] sea into dry land; through the river they passed on foot; there let us rejoice in him.

en.L: He turned [the] sea into dry land; through the river they passed on foot; there let us rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He changed the sea into dry ground; they crossed the river on foot. There let us rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!
en.R: He made the sea into dry land, and they walked through the river on their own feet. Let us be full of joy in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as they were there!

decisions.choice: the sea and the river: the Red Sea and the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel crossed the sea on dry ground when leaving Egypt (Exodus 14:21-22) and crossed the Jordan when entering the land (Joshua 3:14-17). The two crossings frame the whole journey from slavery to the promised land, as in 114:3-5.

decisions.choice: there let us rejoice: the singers join the crossing
decisions.reason: The verb has the form "let us rejoice", but "there" points back to the crossing. The worshipers count themselves among the people who crossed, as if they had been there. Some take it as a past statement, "there we rejoiced".

decisions.choice: as they were there
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear how "there" fits (m2).

source.text: מֹ֘שֵׁ֤ל בִּגְבוּרָת֨וֹ׀עוֹלָ֗ם עֵ֭ינָיו בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם תִּצְפֶּ֑ינָה הַסּוֹרְרִ֓ים׀אַל־יָר֖וּמוּ לָ֣מוֹ סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: [He is] ruling by his might forever; his eyes keep watch on the nations; the rebellious, let them not exalt themselves. Selah.

en.L: [He is] ruling by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} might forever; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes keep watch on the nations; the rebellious, let them not exalt themselves. Selah
en.B: He reigns in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power forever, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes watch closely over the nations. Let no rebels raise themselves up. Selah
en.R: He rules forever with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power. His eyes are always on the nations. People who rebel had better not think they are great. Selah

decisions.choice: let them not exalt themselves: the word as read
decisions.reason: The words follow the form the Hebrew text's notes say to read, "be exalted"; the written form means "raise up". The meaning is the same: the rebels are warned not to rise in pride.

decisions.choice: keep watch: look out like a watchman
decisions.reason: The verb (tsafah) is the work of a lookout on a wall. Nothing the nations do escapes God's sight.

decisions.choice: themselves
decisions.reason: The small word at the end (lamo) is "for them", that is, "themselves". Some read it as rising up against God.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: בָּרְכ֖וּ עַמִּ֥ים׀אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְ֝הַשְׁמִ֗יעוּ ק֣וֹל תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Bless, peoples, our God, and make heard [the] sound of his praise,

en.L: Bless, peoples, our God, and make heard the sound of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise,
en.B: Peoples of the world, bless our God, and make the sound of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise ring out,
en.R: All you nations, praise our God! Let everyone hear you praising {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} loudly.

decisions.choice: bless: praise and thank God
decisions.reason: When people bless God (barak), they speak well of him with thanks and praise (16:7; 34:2).

decisions.choice: the call widens to the peoples
decisions.reason: The peoples of the earth are called to praise the God of Israel, "our God", for what he has done for his people.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 9 says who this God is, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: הַשָּׂ֣ם נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ בַּֽחַיִּ֑ים וְלֹֽא־נָתַ֖ן לַמּ֣וֹט רַגְלֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: who placed our soul in life and did not give our foot to slipping.

en.L: who placed our soul among the living and did not give our foot to slipping.
en.B: the one who keeps us alive and has not let our feet stumble.
en.R: He has kept us alive. He has not let us fall.

decisions.choice: placed our soul in life: kept us alive
decisions.reason: Nefesh here is the life of the people; God has kept them among the living through danger.

decisions.choice: our foot slipping: falling into disaster
decisions.reason: A slipping foot is a picture of sudden ruin (38:17; 121:3).

decisions.choice: us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "us" for nefesh, as the convention is.

source.text: כִּֽי־בְחַנְתָּ֥נוּ אֱלֹהִ֑ים צְ֝רַפְתָּ֗נוּ כִּצְרָף־כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: For you have tested us, God; you have refined us as refining silver.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have tested us, God; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have refined us as silver is refined.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have put us to the test, God; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have refined us the way silver is refined.
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have tested us. You have made us pure, the way fire makes silver pure.

decisions.choice: refined: purified by fire
decisions.reason: The verb (tsaraf) is the work of a smelter who melts silver to burn away what is not pure (12:7; Isaiah 48:10; Zechariah 13:9). The hard times of verses 11-12 were God's testing.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for praise
decisions.reason: The psalm now speaks to God and tells why the peoples should praise: God brought his people through testing to safety.

decisions.choice: the way fire makes silver pure
decisions.reason: Readable names the fire that refining needs.

source.text: הֲבֵאתָ֥נוּ בַמְּצוּדָ֑ה שַׂ֖מְתָּ מוּעָקָ֣ה בְמָתְנֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: You brought us into the net; you put [a] crushing load on our hips.

en.L: You brought us into the net; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put a crushing load on our hips.
en.B: You led us into the trap; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} laid a heavy weight on our backs.
en.R: You let us be caught like animals in a net. You loaded us down with heavy troubles.

decisions.choice: the net: a hunter's net or trap
decisions.reason: The word (metsudah) can mean a hunting net or a fortress. With "brought us into" it is a trap or a place of confinement: Israel was caught and held.

decisions.choice: crushing load: a heavy pressure
decisions.reason: The word (mu'aqah) is found only here; it seems to come from a root meaning to press. On the hips or loins, where a load is carried, it is a crushing weight.

decisions.choice: backs
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "hips", where loads were borne; Balanced and Readable use the familiar place for a burden.

source.text: הִרְכַּ֥בְתָּ אֱנ֗וֹשׁ לְרֹ֫אשֵׁ֥נוּ בָּֽאנוּ־בָאֵ֥שׁ וּבַמַּ֑יִם וַ֝תּוֹצִיאֵ֗נוּ לָֽרְוָיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: You made [a] man ride over our head; we went through fire and through water, and you brought us out to saturation.

en.L: You made men ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought us out to overflowing.
en.B: You let mere mortals ride roughshod over our heads; we came through fire and water, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led us out into overflowing plenty.
en.R: You let enemies trample over us. We went through fire and through floods. But then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought us out to a place where we have more than enough.

decisions.choice: ride over our head: be trampled by conquerors
decisions.reason: The picture is of a defeated people lying on the ground while the victors' horses or chariots pass over them (Isaiah 51:23). The word for "man" ('enosh) is a mortal, weak man: God let weak humans walk over his people.

decisions.choice: fire and water: every kind of danger
decisions.reason: Isaiah 43:2 makes the same pair a picture of the worst trials, through which God brings his people.

decisions.choice: saturation: overflowing abundance
alternatives: a place of refreshment (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The word (revayah) means being filled to overflowing, as in 23:5 "my cup overflows". The ancient Greek translation reads "refreshment"; a word with one letter different would mean "relief" or "a wide place".

decisions.choice: enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names who the riders are.

source.text: אָב֣וֹא בֵיתְךָ֣ בְעוֹל֑וֹת אֲשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְךָ֣ נְדָרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I will come [into] your house with burnt offerings; I will pay to you my vows,

en.L: I will come [into] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house with burnt offerings; I will pay {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} my vows,
en.B: I will enter {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house with whole burnt offerings and keep my vows to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},
en.R: I will come to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple with animals to burn on the altar. I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} what I promised.

decisions.choice: the speaker changes to "I"
decisions.reason: From here one worshiper speaks, perhaps a leader speaking for the people, or one person who was rescued and brings thanks.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings: sacrifices burned whole on the altar
decisions.reason: The burnt offering ('olah) was burned entirely as a gift to God (Leviticus 1).

decisions.choice: pay my vows: keep promises made in trouble
decisions.reason: In distress a worshiper might promise an offering to God if rescued (Leviticus 7:16; 22:21). Paying the vow was a public act of thanks.

decisions.choice: animals to burn on the altar
decisions.reason: Readable says what a burnt offering is (m2).

source.text: אֲשֶׁר־פָּצ֥וּ שְׂפָתָ֑י וְדִבֶּר־פִּ֝֗י בַּצַּר־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: which my lips opened and my mouth spoke in the distress of me.

en.L: which my lips opened [to say] and my mouth spoke in my distress.
en.B: the promises that burst from my lips, that my mouth made in my time of distress.
en.R: I made those promises when I was in trouble.

decisions.choice: opened: opened wide, spoke out
decisions.reason: The verb (patsah) means to open the mouth wide; the vows were spoken aloud, perhaps rashly, in the moment of need (Judges 11:35-36).

decisions.choice: the promises
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "which" refers to: the vows of verse 13.

source.text: עֹ֘ל֤וֹת מֵחִ֣ים אַעֲלֶה־לָּ֭ךְ עִם־קְטֹ֣רֶת אֵילִ֑ים אֶ֥עֱשֶֽׂה בָקָ֖ר עִם־עַתּוּדִ֣ים סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Burnt offerings of fatlings I will offer up to you with [the] smoke of rams; I will make cattle with goats. Selah.

en.L: Burnt offerings of fatlings I will offer up to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, with [the] smoke of rams; I will make cattle with goats. Selah
en.B: I will offer {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} burnt offerings of fattened animals, along with the smoke of rams rising to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; I will sacrifice bulls together with goats. Selah
en.R: I will burn the best fattened animals for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. The smoke of rams will rise up to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I will bring {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bulls and goats as well. Selah

decisions.choice: smoke: the smoke rising from the sacrifice
decisions.reason: The word (qetoret) is often used for incense, but here it is the smoke of the burning rams going up to God.

decisions.choice: make: offer as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: The ordinary verb "make, do" (asah) is used for preparing and offering a sacrifice (Exodus 29:36).

decisions.choice: a lavish offering
decisions.reason: Fattened animals, rams, bulls and goats are the costliest offerings. The thanks matches the size of the rescue.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: לְכֽוּ־שִׁמְע֣וּ וַ֭אֲסַפְּרָה כָּל־יִרְאֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשָׂ֣ה לְנַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: Come, hear, and I will recount, all who fear God, what he has done for my soul.

en.L: Come, hear, and I will recount, all who fear God, what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for my soul.
en.B: Come, listen, all who revere God; let me recount the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for me.
en.R: Come and listen, everyone who honors God with awe. I will tell you what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did for me.

decisions.choice: those who fear God: those who worship him
decisions.reason: To fear God is to hold him in reverent awe and so to obey him (34:10, 12). Here they are the worshiping community gathered to hear the testimony.

decisions.choice: come, hear: a second invitation
decisions.reason: The call of verse 5, "Come and see", is now "Come and listen": first the nation's story, now one person's.

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "me" for nefesh.

source.text: אֵלָ֥יו פִּֽי־קָרָ֑אתִי וְ֝רוֹמַ֗ם תַּ֣חַת לְשׁוֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: To him [with] my mouth I called, and exaltation [was] under my tongue.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [with] my mouth I called, and exaltation [was] under my tongue.
en.B: With my own mouth I called to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and praise to lift {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} high was ready under my tongue.
en.R: I called out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for help. Even while I prayed, I was ready to praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: under my tongue: ready to be spoken
decisions.reason: What is under the tongue is close at hand to say (10:7). Praise was already on the way while the psalmist was still crying for help.

decisions.choice: exaltation: praise that lifts God high
decisions.reason: The word (romam) is from the verb "be high"; it is praise that exalts God (149:6).

decisions.choice: for help
decisions.reason: Readable says what the call was.

source.text: אָ֭וֶן אִם־רָאִ֣יתִי בְלִבִּ֑י לֹ֖א יִשְׁמַ֣ע׀אֲדֹנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Wickedness, if I had seen [it] in my heart, not would he listen, [the] Lord.

en.L: Wickedness, if I had seen [it] in my heart, the Lord would not listen.
en.B: The Lord would not have heard me if I had kept wrongdoing in my heart.
en.R: The Lord would not have listened to me if I had loved my sin and kept it.

decisions.choice: seen wickedness in my heart: cherished it
decisions.reason: To see something in the heart is to look on it with favor and hold on to it. The psalmist claims no sinlessness, only that he did not pray while clinging to evil (Isaiah 59:2; Proverbs 28:9).

decisions.choice: if I had: a condition that did not happen
decisions.reason: The "if" describes what was not the case: verse 19 says God did hear.

decisions.choice: the Lord: 'Adonai
decisions.reason: The title 'Adonai ("my Lord") names God as master.

decisions.choice: the Lord would not have heard me if ...
alternatives: if I had cherished wickedness in my heart ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the main clause first for a clear sentence.

source.text: אָ֭כֵן שָׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהִ֑ים הִ֝קְשִׁ֗יב בְּק֣וֹל תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: But truly God has heard; he has paid attention to [the] voice of my prayer.

en.L: But truly God has heard; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has paid attention to the voice of my prayer.
en.B: Yet God has indeed heard me; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has paid close attention as I prayed.
en.R: But God did listen! He heard me when I prayed.

decisions.choice: but truly: but in fact
decisions.reason: The word ('aken) affirms strongly against what might have been: God did hear.

decisions.choice: paid attention: listened closely
decisions.reason: The verb (qashav, causative) is to give attention with the ear (5:3).

source.text: בָּר֥וּךְ אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־הֵסִ֘יר תְּפִלָּתִ֥י וְ֝חַסְדּ֗וֹ מֵאִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be] God, who has not turned aside my prayer and his loyal love from me.

en.L: Blessed [be] God, who has not turned aside my prayer, nor {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love from me!
en.B: Blessed be God, who has not pushed my prayer aside or taken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love away from me!
en.R: Praise God! He did not turn away from my prayer, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has not stopped loving me faithfully.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that keeps faith within a bond: the LORD's committed, dependable kindness to his people. Literal and Balanced say "loyal love".

decisions.choice: turned aside my prayer and his love: one verb for both
decisions.reason: The one verb "turned aside" governs both: God did not reject the prayer, and did not withdraw his loyal love.

decisions.choice: blessed be God: praise to God
decisions.reason: The psalm ends as it began, with praise, now from one who was heard.

decisions.choice: loving me faithfully
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words for chesed.
